claims: The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall.
The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is the most powerful rocket in operation.
The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket produces 8.8 million pounds of thrust at launch.
The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is designed to carry four astronauts in the Orion capsule around the Moon.
The orange core stage of the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is 212 feet (65 meters) tall.
The two white solid rocket boosters of the Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket stand 177 feet (54 meters) tall.
The Orion capsule is 11 feet high.
The Orion capsule is 16.5 feet wide.
The Orion capsule offers about 330 cubic feet of habitable space for the four crew members.
The Artemis II Space Launch System (SLS) rocket has a liftoff weight of 2,600 tonnes (5.76 million lbs).
The SLS rocket is shorter than the 363-foot Apollo-era Saturn V.
The SLS rocket is more powerful than the Apollo-era Saturn V.
